system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
The Seller’s **[STANDARD]** and **FINAL** labels are advocacy, not evidence of agreement. Review all provisions against the signed deal terms and underlying DD documents; the supplied summaries do not establish that the buyer accepted these positions.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What the buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 General liability cap** | General warranty claims capped at **AUD 4.8m (20% of price)**. | A materially higher cap, opening at **100% of price**, with adequate credit support and separate treatment for fundamental claims and indemnities. | **Reject 20%** pending assessment of the actual risk allocation; it leaves most of the AUD 24m investment unprotected. |
| **SPA-N-002 De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 per-claim floor; AUD 250,000 basket, recoverable only above the basket. | Lower or no per-claim floor, aggregation of related losses, and a **tipping** basket under which all qualifying losses become recoverable once crossed. | **Counter the deductible basket and aggregation rules**; multiple related losses should not be stranded below artificial thresholds. |
| **SPA-N-003 General claims time limit** | General warranty claims notified within 18 months; limits purportedly extend to all claims unless excepted. | At least **24 months** for general warranties, with separate longer periods for tax, IP and fundamental matters, and adequate time to pursue notified claims. | **Reject the all-claims extension**; important liabilities may emerge after 18 months. |
| **SPA-N-004 Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title subject to general cap and time limit. | Separate fundamental warranties covering authority, ownership, issued capital and unencumbered transfer; liability up to at least the **full price**, with a substantially longer claim period and no basket. | **Carve fundamental claims out of the general regime**; defective title strikes at the asset being purchased. |
| **SPA-N-005 Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to *all* claims; no express fraud exception is offered. | Express preservation of remedies for fraud, dishonesty, deliberate concealment and non-excludable statutory rights, notwithstanding any cap, time bar, disclosure or non-reliance term. | **Add an overriding carve-out**; the Seller must not benefit from limitations where it has deliberately misled the buyer. |
| **SPA-N-006 Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the entire data room, accounts, registers and public records. | Only matters **fairly, specifically and sufficiently disclosed** against identified warranties, with enough detail to assess nature and likely impact; no general data-room or public-record sweep. | **Reject blanket disclosure**; mere document availability should not extinguish a warranty claim. |
| **SPA-N-007 Buyer knowledge qualifier** | Claims barred for buyer/adviser knowledge, including matters discoverable in the data room or public records. | Prefer no knowledge bar; if unavoidable, limit it to **actual knowledge of named buyer individuals** at signing, excluding constructive, imputed and adviser knowledge. | **Delete or tightly narrow clause 8.3**; “discoverable” shifts the Seller’s warranty risk to the buyer. |
| **SPA-N-008 Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied on delivery of written consent, although DD-002 conditions are not shown satisfied. | A genuine condition precedent requiring final effective consent **and satisfaction or waiver acceptable to buyer of clause 11.3 conditions**, before Completion, with buyer termination rights. | **Do not treat a bare consent letter as sufficient**; Bluefen represents about AUD 3.6m, or 30%, of FY26 revenue. |
| **SPA-N-009 Riverlark facility** | Approximately AUD 3.2m facility; security release to follow Completion. | Repayment from Seller proceeds **at Completion**, bank payout evidence, binding release/discharge deliverables and funds-flow treatment consistent with debt-free/cash-free pricing. | **Reject post-Completion release as the sole protection**; buyer should not acquire the shares subject to unresolved debt or security. |
| **SPA-N-010 Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 conditional Completion bonuses omitted from funds flow; on-costs unresolved. | Seller-funded payment or full price deduction/escrow for bonuses and applicable superannuation, payroll tax and other on-costs, with clear allocation of employee obligations. | **Add the amount and on-costs to funds flow**; Completion-triggered liabilities must not silently reduce buyer value. |
| **SPA-N-011 Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity confined to the specific SOW3 payment; AUD 180,000 remains open and assignment is unconfirmed. | Cleared payment and confirmatory assignment/ownership evidence before Completion, plus a standalone indemnity for all loss arising from unpaid fees or defective IP title, outside general limitations. | **Expand the protection and obtain title evidence**; paying AUD 180,000 alone may not establish ownership of the Project Materials. |
| **SPA-N-012 Export/privacy incident** | DD-006 treated as preliminary and not expected to be material; access, scope and notification remain unresolved. | Prompt investigation and evidence preservation, buyer-approved remediation and notifications, a bring-down update before Completion, and a specific indemnity/escrow for this pre-Completion incident. | **Keep the issue open despite disclosure**; uncertainty about access to roughly 1,240 records is a risk, not a clean bill of health. |
| **SPA-N-013 Sandbar renewals** | Three AUD 110,000 renewals characterised as ordinary-course costs. | Review DD-008 and DD-011 together for timing, scope, termination and accrual; allocate pre-Completion obligations to Seller and address unusual post-Completion commitments in price or covenants. | **Do not accept the label without verification**; the aggregate AUD 330,000 exposure may alter the agreed economics. |
| **SPA-N-014 Category separation** | Caps, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance drafted to reach all claims unless expressly excepted. | An express claims hierarchy separating general warranties from fundamental/title, tax, IP, specific indemnities, covenants, completion obligations, price adjustments and fraud. | **Redraft each limitation by claim category**; otherwise the general regime can swallow specifically negotiated protections. |
| **SPA-N-015 Title verification** | Seller relies on DD-012 share register showing it holds 100%. | Verify issued capital and rights to shares through corporate records, share instruments, options/convertibles, approvals and searches; require valid transfers and release of any share security at Completion. | **Do not rely on the register alone**; it does not by itself prove clean, transferable title to all equity. |
| **SPA-N-016 Tax/IP open terms** | Seller says tax and IP warranties are settled under the general 20%/18-month regime. | Separate robust tax and IP warranties, appropriate longer claim periods, specific indemnities for identified exposures, and caps appropriate to their risk rather than the general regime. | **Reopen both categories**; tax exposure and core software ownership can outlast and exceed the proposed general protections. |

**Priority for mark-up:** Bluefen condition, Riverlark repayment and releases, Ironquay IP title, the incident, and the all-claims limitation architecture. The Disclosure Letter’s own reservations and gaps reinforce that these matters remain unresolved.
=== END ADVICE ===
